issues.body: In plan_renewal(), state == "unknown" for an expired row appends the lease byte-identically. Its expires_at remains <= now. As this diff itself correctly documents, reclaim_expired(), partition_available(), _live_holder_keys(), and sibling_lease_conflict all treat such a row as absent. Therefore a transient 403/5xx/malformed response does not actually defer the ownership decision: it immediately makes the account/holder eligible to other dispatchers while the original run may still be active. This recreates the double-dispatch bug whenever the liveness API is unavailable. The self-test `an UNPROVEN probe defers the row unchanged` is vacuous with respect to the safety claim because it asserts row presence, not that any real suppression consumer sees the row as live; the e2e unknown test similarly asserts only no PUT.
issues.fix_hint: For an expired due row whose liveness is unknown and whose timestamps/run binding are otherwise valid and below the absolute ceiling, preserve effective exclusivity by moving expires_at to a short, ceiling-clamped retry/grace deadline (or otherwise make every suppression consumer treat the deferred row as live). Add a red test that passes the unknown-path output through reclaim_expired/partition or the dispatch live-holder logic and proves it still suppresses a competing claim. Keep the absolute ceiling so repeated probe failure remains bounded.
issues.title: Unknown liveness leaves an expired lease fail-open to duplicate dispatch

verdict.summary: The liveness-aware reclaim has a blocking fail-open path: when the Actions probe is unavailable or returns an unrecognized response, an already-expired lease is retained without extending its expiry. All duplicate-suppression consumers intentionally ignore that row because they require expires_at > now, so the holder can be dispatched a second time during the exact API-failure case called "deferred." The new tests encode the unsafe behavior and never exercise the retained row through a suppression consumer.
